IIB-F051: Scope of the generated tests on a finite carrier

Claim p2:rem:generated-test-scope. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2165–2206; original complete lines 2164–2205.

Current source object

\begin{remark}[Scope of the generated tests on a finite carrier]
\label{p2:rem:generated-test-scope}
The theorem above classifies invariant positive normalized functionals on the
full algebra \(\End(V)\).  For the block embedding
\(\iota_\lambda(A)\), equal to
\(A\otimes\mathbf1_{M_\lambda}\) on the \(\lambda\)-block and zero on all
other blocks, put
\[
 P_\lambda:=\iota_\lambda(I_{V_\lambda}),
 \qquad
 p_\lambda:=\tau(P_\lambda)
 =(\dim V_\lambda)\Tr_{M_\lambda}(B_\lambda).
\]
Then the exact block formula is
\[
 \tau\!\left(\iota_\lambda(A)\right)
 =p_\lambda\frac{\Tr_{V_\lambda}(A)}{\dim V_\lambda}.
\]
Only after conditioning on a sector of positive weight does the sector weight
cancel:
\[
 \frac{\tau(\iota_\lambda(A))}{\tau(P_\lambda)}
 =\frac{\Tr_{V_\lambda}(A)}{\dim V_\lambda},
 \qquad p_\lambda>0.
\]

The unmarked finite-role doctrine of
Proposition~\ref{p2:prop:gp3-multiplicity-bound} uses the observable algebra
\[
 \mathcal A_{\rm unmarked}
 =\bigoplus_\lambda
 \End(V_\lambda)\otimes\mathbf1_{M_\lambda}.
\]
Restrictions of invariant states to this algebra retain the free sector
weights \(p_\lambda\) but cannot distinguish directions inside
\(M_\lambda\).  A state on the full \(\End(V)\) can distinguish such
directions only through observables acting nontrivially on \(M_\lambda\); the
unmarked hypothesis excludes those observables rather than silently replacing
the sector weight by one.  Finally, \(\tau(\mathbf1)=1\) for every state, so
normalization alone does not return the carrier dimension.  This fixes the
scope of ``generated test'' used in that proposition.
\end{remark}

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

IIB-F052: Full basis neutrality is an additional hypothesis

Claim p2:rem:no-insertion-basis-neutrality. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2208–2214; original complete lines 2207–2213.

Current source object

\begin{remark}[Full basis neutrality is an additional hypothesis]
\label{p2:rem:no-insertion-basis-neutrality}
The absence of a preferred basis does not enlarge a constituted symmetry
group to \(U(V)\).  Full-unitary invariance is a sufficient extra hypothesis
for the normalized trace; it is not a consequence of \(G\)-equivariance on a
reducible carrier.
\end{remark}

IIB-F053: Retained Peter--Weyl symbol spaces

Claim p2:def:retained-pw-symbols. Status FORMALIZED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2253–2268; original complete lines 2252–2267.

Current source object

\begin{definition}[Retained Peter--Weyl symbol spaces]
\label{p2:def:retained-pw-symbols}
For each level $m$, define
\[
\mathcal P_m
:=
\operatorname{span}\Bigl\{D^j_{ab}: j\in \tfrac12\ZZ_{\ge0},\; 2j\le m,\; -j\le a,b\le j\Bigr\}
\subset C^\infty(S^3),
\]
where $D^j_{ab}$ are the matrix coefficients of the spin-$j$ irreducible
representation of $SU(2)\cong S^3$.  This is exactly the retained scalar
diagonal coefficient space
\(\mathcal H_m^{\rm sc}\); it is not the full \(\mathcal H_m\),
\(\mathcal A_m\), or \(\End(\mathcal H_m)\).  Its precise finite-operator
relation is the section/retraction proved next.
\end{definition}

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

IIB-F054: Exact scalar Toeplitz section and symbol retraction

Claim p2:prop:scalar-toeplitz-symbol-retraction. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2270–2345; original complete lines 2269–2344.

Current source object

\begin{proposition}[Exact scalar Toeplitz section and symbol retraction]
\label{p2:prop:scalar-toeplitz-symbol-retraction}
Use the scalar diagonal identification
\[
 \mathcal H_m^{\rm sc}=\mathcal P_m
 \subset L^2(S^3),
\]
and let \(\Pi_m^{\rm sc}:L^2(S^3)\to\mathcal H_m^{\rm sc}\) be
the orthogonal projector.  Let
\(\iota_m^{\rm sc}:\mathcal H_m^{\rm sc}\hookrightarrow\mathcal H_m\)
be the diagonal-sector inclusion and
\(r_m^{\rm sc}:\mathcal H_m\to\mathcal H_m^{\rm sc}\) its orthogonal
projection.  For \(f\in\mathcal P_m\), define the scalar-block Toeplitz
section
\[
 Q_m^{\rm sc}(f)
 :=
 \iota_m^{\rm sc}\Pi_m^{\rm sc}M_f r_m^{\rm sc}
 \in\End(\mathcal H_m),
\]
where \(M_f\) is scalar multiplication on \(L^2(S^3)\).  For
\(A\in\End(\mathcal H_m)\), define the scalar symbol evaluated at the
constant unit
\[
 \sigma_m^{\rm sc}(A)
 :=
 r_m^{\rm sc}A\iota_m^{\rm sc}(1)
 \in\mathcal P_m.
\]
Here \(1\) is the algebraic constant unit.  It has norm one for
probability-normalized Haar measure, whereas for Riemannian volume its norm
is \(\sqrt{V_R}\), with
\(V_R=\operatorname{Vol}(S^3(\Rmom))\).  The written map uses \(1\) in
either convention.  Using the normalized constant \(e_0=V_R^{-1/2}\)
under Riemannian volume instead would require a compensating factor
\(\sqrt{V_R}\) in the symbol map.
Then both maps are linear and \(\Spin(4)\)-equivariant, and
\[
 \sigma_m^{\rm sc}\!\circ Q_m^{\rm sc}
 =
 \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal P_m}.
\]
Consequently \(Q_m^{\rm sc}\) is injective and
\(\sigma_m^{\rm sc}\) is surjective.  This is an exact bridge between the
retained scalar coefficient space and a scalar-supported linear operator
space in
\(\End(\mathcal H_m)\).  It is not a multiplicative embedding, it does not
identify \(\mathcal P_m\) with \(\mathcal A_m\) or
\(\End(\mathcal H_m)\), and it supplies no scalar symbols for the
non-diagonal bundle sectors.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The invariant constant function \(1\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_m\), and
\(\Pi_m^{\rm sc}\) fixes every element of \(\mathcal P_m\).  Therefore, for
each \(f\in\mathcal P_m\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sigma_m^{\rm sc}\!\left(Q_m^{\rm sc}(f)\right)
 &=
 r_m^{\rm sc}\iota_m^{\rm sc}
 \Pi_m^{\rm sc}M_f
 r_m^{\rm sc}\iota_m^{\rm sc}(1)\\
 &=
 \Pi_m^{\rm sc}(f\cdot1)
 =f.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the retraction identity, injectivity, and surjectivity.  The
left--right action preserves the scalar diagonal sector and its orthogonal
complement, fixes \(1\), commutes with \(\Pi_m^{\rm sc}\), and satisfies
\(U_gM_fU_g^{-1}=M_{U_gf}\).  Hence both displayed maps intertwine the
\(\Spin(4)\)-actions.  The remaining boundary statements follow directly
from the types of the maps: no injectivity of the retraction and no
product-preservation property has been imposed.
\end{proof}

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

IIB-F055: Peter--Weyl parent-symbol density from the finite tower

Claim p2:thm:continuum_limit. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2347–2391; original complete lines 2346–2390.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Peter--Weyl parent-symbol density from the finite tower]
\label{p2:thm:continuum_limit}
Let $\mathcal P_m$ be the retained Peter--Weyl coefficient space of Definition~\ref{p2:def:retained-pw-symbols}. Then
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{poly}}:=\bigcup_{m\ge0}\mathcal P_m
\]
is the Peter--Weyl polynomial algebra on $SU(2)$ and is uniformly dense in
$C(S^3)$.  Equivalently, for every \(f\in C(S^3)\),
\[
 \lim_{m\to\infty}
 \inf_{p\in\mathcal P_m}\|f-p\|_\infty=0.
\]
The exact maps in
Proposition~\ref{p2:prop:scalar-toeplitz-symbol-retraction} type the
finite-level scalar coefficient bridge.  The limit is a statement about the
parent presentation and the directed family of finite symbols; no realized
stage has \(m=\infty\).  The conclusion is coefficient-space density only.  It
does not identify finite matrix algebras as literal subalgebras of
\(C(S^3)\), and it is neither an operator-norm nor a dynamical convergence
theorem.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every spin \(j\in\frac12\ZZ_{\ge0}\), choosing any integer \(m\ge 2j\)
places all matrix coefficients \(D^j_{ab}\) in \(\mathcal P_m\).  Hence
\[
\bigcup_m\mathcal P_m
=
\operatorname{span}\{D^j_{ab}:j\in\tfrac12\ZZ_{\ge0},\,-j\le a,b\le j\},
\]
which is precisely the Peter--Weyl polynomial algebra of the compact group
\(SU(2)\).  The Peter--Weyl uniform-density theorem
\cite{Peter1927,helgason1984groups} states that this algebra is dense in
\(C(SU(2))\) in the uniform norm.  After the identification
\(SU(2)\cong S^3\), this gives
\[
\overline{\mathcal P_{\mathrm{poly}}}^{\|\cdot\|_\infty}=C(S^3).
\]
Because the spaces are nested, this closure statement is equivalent to the
displayed limit of best uniform-approximation errors.  The section and
retraction of
Proposition~\ref{p2:prop:scalar-toeplitz-symbol-retraction} do not change the
type of this result: it is not an operator-norm convergence theorem for
\(\mathcal A_m\) or \(\End(\mathcal H_m)\).
\end{proof}

IIB-F056: Mode of convergence

Claim p2:rem:continuum-mode. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2393–2409; original complete lines 2392–2408.

Current source object

\begin{remark}[Mode of convergence]
\label{p2:rem:continuum-mode}
The theorem establishes density of the retained Peter--Weyl symbols in the
classical commutative algebra $C(S^3)$.  This parent-symbol density statement concerns the scalar Peter--Weyl symbol content and is typed as a presentation recovery, not an ontic continuum.  The additional non-diagonal
$(j_L,j_R)$ sectors of the full finite module package require their separate
vector/spinor/bundle interpretation and should not be identified with scalar
functions on $S^3$.  Their share is the larger one: since
$\dim\mathcal P_m=(m+1)(m+2)(2m+3)/6$ and
$\dim\mathcal H_m=\binom{2m+4}{4}$,
\[
 \frac{\dim\mathcal P_m}{\dim\mathcal H_m}=\frac{1}{2m+1},
\]
so the density statement addresses a fraction of the carrier that falls to
zero as the level grows.  More refined semiclassical convergence statements require
additional product, norm, and asymptotic estimates; the exact finite-level
section/retraction above does not supply them by itself.
\end{remark}

IIB-F057: Exact ordered-word defect and its bound

Claim p2b:thm:v2210-lit-word-defect. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2425–2464; original complete lines 2424–2463.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Exact ordered-word defect and its bound]
\label{p2b:thm:v2210-lit-word-defect}
Let $P=P^\dagger=P^2$, $Q=I-P$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be bounded
operators on a supplied common parent, $n\ge2$.  On $P\mathcal H$, put
\[
 W_P=(PA_1P)\cdots(PA_nP),\qquad W=P A_1\cdots A_n P.
\]
Then exactly
\[
 W-W_P=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}
 (PA_1P)\cdots(PA_{j-1}P)\,PA_jQ A_{j+1}\cdots A_nP,
\]
where the prefix is the identity on $P\mathcal H$ when $j=1$.  Consequently
\[
 \|W-W_P\|\le\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}
 \left(\prod_{i<j}\|A_i\|\right)
 \|PA_jQ\|\,\|QA_{j+1}\cdots A_nP\|.
\]
For a supplied isometry $Z$ with $P=ZZ^\dagger$, define
$\pi_Z(A)=Z^\dagger AZ$.  Its positive square defect and mixed defect obey
\[
 D_Z(A):=\pi_Z(A^\dagger A)-\pi_Z(A)^\dagger\pi_Z(A)
 =(QAZ)^\dagger(QAZ),
 \qquad \|D_Z(A)\|=\|QAZ\|^2,
\]
\[
 \|\pi_Z(AB)-\pi_Z(A)\pi_Z(B)\|
 \le\|QA^\dagger Z\|\,\|QBZ\|.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Insert $I=P+Q$ at the first internal interface of $W$, and repeat only on
the term whose retained prefix still ends in $P$.  This partitions the
difference by the first omitted intermediate image, giving the exact sum.
Submultiplicativity gives the bound.  The square and mixed identities
follow by inserting $ZZ^\dagger=P$ between the compressed factors, as in
Paper~I-B, Lemma~\ref{p1b:lem:v2167-compression-multiplication}.
For the square, $T^\dagger T$ has norm $\|T\|^2$; for the mixed defect
use $Z^\dagger AQBZ=(QA^\dagger Z)^\dagger(QBZ)$.
\end{proof}

Consequently\n\\[\n \\|W-W_P\\|\\le\\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\n \\left(\\prod_{i<j}\\|A_i\\|\\right)\n \\|PA_jQ\\|\\,\\|QA_{j+1}\\cdots A_nP\\|.\n\\]"
      }

IIB-F058: A consumed comparison needs only its visible defect

Claim p2b:cor:v2210-lit-visible-word-defect. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2466–2486; original complete lines 2465–2485.

Current source object

\begin{corollary}[A consumed comparison needs only its visible defect]
\label{p2b:cor:v2210-lit-visible-word-defect}
For normalized source vectors $u,v\in P\mathcal H$ or a density operator
$\sigma$ on that range,
\[
 |u^\dagger(W-W_P)v|\le\|W-W_P\|,
 \qquad |\operatorname{Tr}\sigma(W-W_P)|\le\|W-W_P\|.
\]
Exact reduction of the consumed parent algebra makes all defects zero.
An observable-specific zero contraction can suffice for that comparison
without proving reduction of every mathematically available parent word.
If source derivatives are consumed, the same test applies separately to
the actual differentiated word, including derivatives of $P$ or $Z$ when
the retained chart moves.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The first inequality is the operator norm estimate, and the second follows
from positivity and unit trace.  Reduction annihilates $PAQ$ and $QAP$.
The final assertion is application of the same identities to the fully
differentiated supplied word, not deletion of chart-derivative terms.
\end{proof}

IIB-U009: D01 full pointwise scalar products and harmonic capacity

Claim BH-IIB-CENSUS-U009. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2515–2546; original complete lines 2514–2545.

Current source object

The scalar constant and degree-one harmonics occur in the retained carrier.
If a downstream constructor licenses their \emph{full pointwise product},
it must retain the nine-dimensional degree-two scalar harmonic output.
For ambient scalar coordinates on $S^3(R)$,
\[
 x_ax_b=\frac{R^2}{4}\delta_{ab}
 +\left(x_ax_b-\frac{R^2}{4}\delta_{ab}\right),\qquad
 \dim E_2=9.
\]
The second term is the symmetric traceless quadratic sector. More generally,
products of at most $r$ degree-one functions span
\[
 \bigoplus_{\ell=0}^r E_\ell,
 \qquad \dim=\sum_{\ell=0}^r(\ell+1)^2
 =\frac{(r+1)(r+2)(2r+3)}6.
\]
Here $E_\ell$ is the degree-$\ell$ scalar harmonic eigenspace.
It is not the full auxiliary module $\mathcal H_\ell$; in particular
$\dim E_2=9$ whereas $\dim\mathcal H_2=\binom84=70$.
\begin{proof}
Restrict homogeneous polynomials to the sphere and remove their
Euclidean traces. Each polynomial decomposes into harmonic polynomials times
powers of $|x|^2$, which become constants on the sphere. Conversely the
coordinate monomials generate every such polynomial. The symmetric
quadratic tensors have dimension ten, with one trace.
\end{proof}
Thus linear/bracket closure of the 15-dimensional one-copy module is not closure
under all pointwise products. Projected operator composition and full
function multiplication are different words; a finite matrix algebra can
close under the former without acquiring the latter's harmonic outputs.
This is a capacity result, not a license to enlarge the physical carrier. The exact omitted-image error for each actually licensed retained word is now given by Theorem~\ref{p2b:thm:v2210-lit-word-defect}; its source-visible contraction remains the application calculation.
\par\noindent\textit{Inherited inputs:} \ref{p2:thm:momentum-host-H1}, \ref{p2b:thm:momentum-carrier-rigidity}, \ref{p3f:thm:v180-incidence-harmonic-resolution}.

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

IIB-F059: No finite covariant multiplicative sphere realization

Claim p2b:thm:finite-covariant-classical-algebra-obstruction. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2548–2578; original complete lines 2547–2577.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[No finite covariant multiplicative sphere realization]
\label{p2b:thm:finite-covariant-classical-algebra-obstruction}
Let a group $G$ act transitively by homeomorphisms on an infinite compact Hausdorff space $X$,
and let $U$ be a unitary representation on a nonzero finite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $H$.  There is no unital $G$-equivariant
$*$-homomorphism
\[
 \pi:C(X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}(H),\qquad
 \pi(f\circ g^{-1})=U_g\pi(f)U_g^*.
\]
In particular, the round $\Spin(4)$ action on $S^3$ admits no such finite
realization.  Every finite unital covariant positive linear map from its
full continuous function algebra must therefore fail multiplicativity on
some pair of functions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The finite-dimensional commutative $C^*$-algebra $\pi(C(X))$ is simultaneously
diagonalizable.  Its distinct characters are evaluations at finitely many
points $x_1,\ldots,x_N\in X$, so
\[
 \pi(f)=\sum_{j=1}^N f(x_j)P_j,
 \qquad P_j\ne0,\quad \sum_jP_j=I.
\]
The kernel consists precisely of functions vanishing on the nonempty finite
support $F=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}$.  Equivariance preserves this kernel and hence
preserves $F$.  Transitivity forces every nonempty invariant subset to equal
$X$, contradicting its infinitude.  A unital positive map on $C(X)$ respects
complex conjugation; if it were multiplicative everywhere, it would be the
forbidden $*$-homomorphism.
\end{proof}

IIB-F060: Structural defect and the frozen carrier

Claim p2b:rem:finite-covariant-defect-scope. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2580–2591; original complete lines 2579–2590.

Current source object

\begin{remark}[Structural defect and the frozen carrier]
\label{p2b:rem:finite-covariant-defect-scope}
The obstruction explains why the product outputs in D01 and the word defect
in Theorem~\ref{p2b:thm:v2210-lit-word-defect} cannot all disappear in a finite
round-covariant function realization.  It does not prohibit exactness on a
specified finite test space, finite sampling without the full continuous
group action, or closure under matrix multiplication.  Nor does it select a
particular POVM map or enlarge the frozen momentum carrier.  Paper II-C's
optimal coordinate POVMs realize the positive-map alternative; their
remaining family freedom must be retained by a downstream prediction that
consumes classical quadratic readouts.
\end{remark}

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

IIB-F061: Degree six is an operation bound, not a momentum level

Claim p2b:cor:v226-coordinate-word-degree. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2598–2615; original complete lines 2597–2614.

Current source object

\begin{corollary}[Degree six is an operation bound, not a momentum level]
\label{p2b:cor:v226-coordinate-word-degree}
On the generated intrinsic class define
$\mathcal W_d=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{I,Y_{a_1}\cdots Y_{a_s}:s\le d\}$.
Then $\dim\mathcal W_5=136$ and
$\mathcal W_6=\mathcal A_D$ has dimension 137. The intrinsic coordinate-word calculation here acts on the explicit
one-copy module $\mathcal H_1$ of dimension fifteen; universal
identification with every GP3 physical endpoint retains the additional
comparison hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{p2b:thm:momentum-carrier-rigidity}.
The label $d$ here is not the carrier tensor-word level $m$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The degree-six identity and explicit degree-five obstruction are
Theorem~\ref{p1:thm:v226-chirality}; the exact rank certificate gives the
lower dimension 136. These are products of represented endomorphisms on
one carrier, not an insertion of a new representation sector. The frozen
seed frontier and its no-insertion theorem therefore retain their domain.
\end{proof}

IIB-F062: Reverse rigidity of the native $15/137$ data

Claim p2b:thm:v264-algebra-rigidity. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2640–2668; original complete lines 2639–2667.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Reverse rigidity of the native $15/137$ data]
\label{p2b:thm:v264-algebra-rigidity}
If $\mathcal A\subseteq M_{15}(\CC)$ is a \emph{unital complex
finite-dimensional $C^*$-subalgebra} with
$\dim_{\CC}\mathcal A=137$, then its represented form is, up to a
unitary change of basis,
\[
 \boxed{\mathcal A=M_{11}(\CC)\oplus M_4(\CC)}
\]
with each simple block represented once.  Neither the original
coordinate-graph constructor nor its occurring action/readout ownership
follows from these two numbers alone.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Write the faithful unital representation as
$\mathcal A\cong\bigoplus_i M_{n_i}(\CC)$ on
$\bigoplus_i(\CC^{n_i}\otimes\CC^{m_i})$, where $m_i\ge1$.
Then $\sum_i n_i^2=137$ and $\sum_i n_im_i=15$.
If every $n_i\le9$, then
$137=\sum_i n_i^2\le9\sum_i n_i\le135$, impossible.
Also $n_i\le11$ because $12^2>137$. If a largest block has
$n_i=10$, the remaining blocks have total defining dimension at most
five and therefore total squared dimension at most $5^2=25$, whereas
$137-100=37$ is required. Hence a largest block is $11$.
The remaining blocks have total defining dimension at most four and
squared dimension $137-121=16$, which forces precisely one block of
size four. These two blocks exhaust the $15$ representation dimensions,
so both multiplicities are one.
\end{proof}

IIB-F063: Inverse quadratic fingerprint within the coordinate atlas

Claim p2b:prop:v264-quadratic-inversion. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2670–2699; original complete lines 2669–2698.

Current source object

\begin{proposition}[Inverse quadratic fingerprint within the coordinate atlas]
\label{p2b:prop:v264-quadratic-inversion}
Fix the normalized Hermitian equivariant coordinate-completion atlas
of Paper~I-A with $R_{\rm mom}>0$ and nonnegative reduced magnitudes
$(r_{1,0},r_{0,1},\varrho_{\rm sp})$. Denote the scalar, vector, left
bivector, right bivector, and spinor eigenvalues of
$Q=\sum_{a=1}^{4}X_a^2$ by $(q_0,q_V,q_L,q_R,q_S)$.
Within this declared atlas, their exact inverse is
\[
\boxed{R_{\rm mom}=\sqrt{q_0},\quad
r_{1,0}=\sqrt{q_L/2},\quad r_{0,1}=\sqrt{q_R/2},\quad
\varrho_{\rm sp}=\tfrac12\sqrt{q_S}},
\qquad
\boxed{q_V=\tfrac14q_0+\tfrac34(q_L+q_R)}.
\]
Thus nonnegative sector data satisfying the last identity reconstruct
all reduced magnitudes modulo the atlas's phase equivalence. Outside
the stipulated atlas, neither the same fingerprint nor the same abstract
algebra reconstructs the coordinate operator or its action provenance.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The fixed scalar/vector edge and outgoing-path trace identities
of Paper~I-A give
$q_0=R_{\rm mom}^2$, $q_L=2r_{1,0}^2$,
$q_R=2r_{0,1}^2$, $q_S=4\varrho_{\rm sp}^2$ and
$q_V=R_{\rm mom}^2/4+\tfrac32(r_{1,0}^2+r_{0,1}^2)$.
Solving gives the claimed necessary and sufficient algebraic relations
inside that atlas. Existence and phase classification are inherited
from the specified atlas, not inferred for arbitrary operator tuples.
\end{proof}

IIB-F064: Explicit central grading as a coordinate word

Claim p2b:cor:v264-central-polynomial. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2701–2723; original complete lines 2700–2722.

Current source object

\begin{corollary}[Explicit central grading as a coordinate word]
\label{p2b:cor:v264-central-polynomial}
On the \emph{already generated} intrinsic fixed-radius class of
Paper~II-C, put $q=Q_D/R_{\rm mom}^2$. Then
\[
 q=P_0+\frac{11}{12}P_V+\frac49P_B+\frac34P_S,
\quad
\boxed{P_S=\frac{864}{11}(q-I)
 (q-\tfrac{11}{12}I)(q-\tfrac49I),\quad
 \Gamma_c=I-2P_S.}
\]
Consequently $P_S$ and $\Gamma_c$ are polynomials of coordinate-word
degree at most six; no new operator \emph{choice} is needed on this branch.
A performed measurement of $P_S$ still needs an actual readout/test token.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The fingerprint is Paper~II-C's intrinsic coordinate theorem.
Its four distinct eigenvalues permit Lagrange interpolation at
$3/4$, with denominator
$(3/4-1)(3/4-11/12)(3/4-4/9)=11/864$.
The grading acts as $+1$ on the rank-$11$ complement and $-1$ on
its rank-$4$ spinor block. Each $Q_D$ uses two coordinate factors.
\end{proof}

IIB-F065: Full spinorial representation content of the odd bridge

Claim p2b:thm:v264-odd-bridge-types. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2725–2759; original complete lines 2724–2758.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Full spinorial representation content of the odd bridge]
\label{p2b:thm:v264-odd-bridge-types}
For the derived carrier, write
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal H_g&=(0,0)\oplus(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)
  \oplus(1,0)\oplus(0,1),\\
\mathcal H_s&=(\tfrac12,0)\oplus(0,\tfrac12).
\end{split}
\]
Then as $\Spin(4)$ modules,
\[
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H_s,\mathcal H_g)
 \cong{}&3(\tfrac12,0)\oplus3(0,\tfrac12)\\
 &\oplus2(1,\tfrac12)\oplus2(\tfrac12,1)\\
 &\oplus(\tfrac32,0)\oplus(0,\tfrac32).
\end{aligned}}
\]
It has complex dimension $44$ and no trivial or ordinary-vector
$(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ summand. The self-adjoint off-block operators
form an $88$-real-dimensional space. In particular the irreducible
\emph{type} of a spinorial input leaves three possible channels per
chirality and does not select an action coefficient.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Take the tensor product of $\mathcal H_g$ with the dual of each
half-spinor; all $SU(2)$ finite irreducibles are self-dual. The
Clebsch--Gordan rule
$V_j\otimes V_{1/2}=V_{j-1/2}\oplus V_{j+1/2}$
(with the negative term omitted) gives the displayed multiplicities.
The dimension check is $3(2)+3(2)+2(6)+2(6)+4+4=44$.
The Hermitian odd block is uniquely specified by one $11\times4$
complex matrix and its adjoint, thus has $2(44)=88$ real parameters.
\end{proof}

IIB-F066: Central-even input obstruction and its sharpness

Claim p2b:thm:v264-central-even-no-go. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2761–2788; original complete lines 2760–2787.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Central-even input obstruction and its sharpness]
\label{p2b:thm:v264-central-even-no-go}
Let $z=(-I,-I)\in\Spin(4)$ and let $V$ be any $\Spin(4)$-space on
which $z$ acts trivially. Every $\Spin(4)$-equivariant map
\[
 F:V\longrightarrow
 \mathcal O:=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H_s,\mathcal H_g)
 \oplus\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H_g,\mathcal H_s)
\]
is zero, even if $F$ is nonlinear. Thus wholly central-even
coordinate, tensor, curvature, or bosonic-jet inputs cannot alone
generate a central-odd \emph{one-system} bridge by an equivariant rule.
The obstruction is sharp: for any actual spinorial datum
$0\ne\chi\in\mathcal H_s$ and normalized invariant scalar
$e_0\in\mathcal H_g$, the family
\[
 B_\chi=|e_0\rangle\langle\chi|+|\chi\rangle\langle e_0|
\]
is nonzero, self-adjoint, central-odd and $\Spin(4)$-covariant.
This is mathematical availability only, not physical occurrence.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The central element acts as $+I$ on $\mathcal H_g$ and $-I$ on
$\mathcal H_s$, hence as $-I$ on $\mathcal O$. Equivariance gives
$F(v)=F(zv)=z\cdot F(v)=-F(v)$. For $B_\chi$, the two terms are
adjoint and exchange the blocks; $\Spin(4)$ fixes $e_0$ and sends
$\chi$ to $\rho(g)\chi$, so the claimed covariance follows.
\end{proof}

IIB-F067: No parallel central-odd section for the canonical Born holonomy

Claim p2b:thm:v264-no-parallel-odd. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2790–2820; original complete lines 2789–2819.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[No parallel central-odd section for the canonical Born holonomy]
\label{p2b:thm:v264-no-parallel-odd}
On the associated $\mathcal H_1$ representation bundle for the
\emph{already generated correlated fibre-spin connection} of
Paper~III-F, restrict to its established full $SU(2)_{\rm diag}$
holonomy. Then
\[
\mathcal H_g\!\downarrow_{SU(2)_{\rm diag}}
 =2V_0\oplus3V_1,
\qquad
\mathcal H_s\!\downarrow_{SU(2)_{\rm diag}}=2V_{1/2},
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H_s,\mathcal H_g)
 \!\downarrow_{SU(2)_{\rm diag}}
 =10V_{1/2}\oplus6V_{3/2}.
\]
On any connected domain carrying this holonomy, every parallel odd
section vanishes. This does not rule out nonparallel sections or
create a physical $\mathcal H_1$ interaction bundle from the
fibre connection alone.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Under the diagonal embedding $(j_L,j_R)\downarrow SU(2)$ the vector
$(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ is $V_0\oplus V_1$ and each bivector triplet
is $V_1$. Thus $\mathcal H_g=2V_0\oplus3V_1$;
the chiral doublets are each $V_{1/2}$. Tensoring with two copies
of $V_{1/2}$ gives $2(2V_{1/2}+3(V_{1/2}\oplus V_{3/2}))
=10V_{1/2}\oplus6V_{3/2}$. No trivial summand exists.
A parallel section corresponds to a holonomy-fixed vector, hence is zero.
\end{proof}

IIB-F068: Chiral action oddness is not central-oddness

Claim p2b:prop:v264-chiral-central-distinction. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2822–2841; original complete lines 2821–2840.

Current source object

\begin{proposition}[Chiral action oddness is not central-oddness]
\label{p2b:prop:v264-chiral-central-distinction}
The rooted nonzero $W_L\leftrightarrow W_R$ Dirac coefficient of
Paper~V-A is odd for its \emph{internal chiral} grading but even
under diagonal-center conjugation, since
$\rho_W(z)=-I_W$ on both halves. Moreover its printed action domain
is $\operatorname{End}(W\otimes Q\otimes G)$, not the mixed block
$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal H_s,\mathcal H_g)$.
Therefore its rooted nonzero action incidence by itself does not
discharge the $\mathsf{FENV}$ central-odd bridge or supply a two-carrier
exchange Hessian. This is a type distinction, not a contradiction of
Paper~V-A's nonzero chiral source theorem.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
For every $D_W\in\operatorname{End}(W)$,
$(-I_W)D_W(-I_W)=D_W$; the internal chiral grading need not commute
with $D_W$. The declared source and target spaces of the two
operator owners are distinct, so a nonzero coefficient in the first
is no incidence certificate for the second.
\end{proof}

IIB-F069: Basis-free even paired-odd exchange

Claim p2b:thm:v264-canonical-paired-exchange. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2843–2880; original complete lines 2842–2879.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Basis-free even paired-odd exchange]
\label{p2b:thm:v264-canonical-paired-exchange}
On the \emph{mathematical} two-copy carrier
$\mathcal H_1\otimes\mathcal H_1$, let $F(u\otimes v)=v\otimes u$
be the tensor flip, $P_g,P_s$ the central rank-$11$ and rank-$4$
projectors, and put
\[
 Q_{\times}=P_g\otimes P_s+P_s\otimes P_g,
 \qquad K=FQ_{\times}.
\]
Then
\[
 K^*=K,\quad K^2=Q_{\times},\quad
 \operatorname{rank}K=88,\quad
 [K,\rho(g)\otimes\rho(g)]=0,
\]
\[
 [K,\Gamma_c\otimes\Gamma_c]=0,
 \qquad [K,P_g\otimes I]\ne0.
\]
Thus a symmetry-invariant \emph{total-even} operator can change an
individual carrier's $11/4$ population. It is not in the native
$\mathcal A_{\rm ev}\otimes\mathcal A_{\rm ev}$ test algebra, and
the mathematical tensor construction alone does not actualize a
second carrier, its identification, or an interaction/process token.
The exact conditional population evolution is proved at its
physical-owner boundary in Paper~IV-A.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The flip commutes with the symmetric crossed projector $Q_{\times}$;
both are self-adjoint and $F^2=I$. Therefore $K^*=K$,
$K^2=Q_{\times}$ and its rank is twice $11\cdot4=44$.
The diagonal symmetry and total central parity commute with both
factors. On a vector $u_g\otimes v_s$, $K$ exchanges it with
$v_s\otimes u_g$, so it does not commute with the first system's
$P_g\otimes I$. Every native even tensor-product test does commute
with $P_g\otimes I$, hence $K$ is not one of them.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Non-converses preserved by this reverse audit]
\label{p2b:rem:v264-converse-firewall}
The derived carrier implies $m_p=1$, not conversely: for example
$\mathcal E_9=(0,0)\oplus(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)\oplus
(\tfrac12,0)\oplus(0,\tfrac12)$ also has maximal half-level one.
Likewise $\mathcal H_1$ can be produced abstractly by different
mathematical tensor-prefix/lower-ideal grammars and hence does not
identify its \emph{physical} bracket ancestry. The $15/137$ algebra
and exact quadratic fingerprint are independent reconstruction tests,
not G0 provenance certificates. Nor does a covariant mathematical
exchange imply an action-owned $\mathsf{PROC}$, $\mathsf{DYN}$,
$\mathsf{FENV}$ or $\mathsf{ENV}$ occurrence.
\end{remark}

IIB-F071: No dimension-based carrier identification

Claim p2b:prop:v318-petersen-vs-h1. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 2902–2932; original complete lines 2901–2931.

Current source object

\begin{proposition}[No dimension-based carrier identification]
\label{p2b:prop:v318-petersen-vs-h1}
On the conditional embedded $2I$ support of Paper~II-A, the real
Petersen-edge module $W_P\cong\mathbb R^{15}$ has an $A_5$ action and
a finite decomposition
\[
 W_P\cong\mathbf4\oplus\mathbf5\oplus\mathbf3\oplus\mathbf3'.
\]
It is not the independently generated fifteen-complex-dimensional
round-host momentum carrier
\[
 \mathcal H_1\cong\mathbf1\oplus S\oplus\mathfrak c_{\mathbb C}
 \quad(15=1+4+10)
\]
and it is not the distinct fifteen-dimensional Bose--Mesner block
inside $\mathbb C^{2T}$.  The central binary element $-1\in2I$ acts
trivially on $W_P$; the signed Hopf-axis and quaternionic-fibre
lifts must be retained separately if spinorial central parity is to
be detected.  Neither matching dimension nor restriction of a
continuous representation to a finite subgroup supplies a canonical
intertwining map between these three carriers.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The three spaces are defined on different source objects and with
different actions.  Paper~I-A gives the Petersen representation, and
the round-parent generator/gradient/field-bracket construction here
gives $\mathcal H_1$ independently of any finite subgroup selection.
The $A_5$ permutation action factors through the quotient by the
binary center.  Without a separately owned action-intertwiner, no
identification is licensed by GP2's exact/faithful requirement.
\end{proof}

IIB-F073: Faithful module and commutant characterization

Claim p2b:thm:v352-minimal-faithful. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 3085–3111; original complete lines 3084–3110.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Faithful module and commutant characterization]
\label{p2b:thm:v352-minimal-faithful}
For $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}M_{d_i}(\mathbb C)$, every
finite-dimensional faithful unital $*$-representation is of the form
\[
 \pi(\mathcal A)=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}
     \bigl(M_{d_i}(\mathbb C)\otimes I_{m_i}\bigr),\quad m_i\geq1,
 \qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H=\sum_i d_i m_i.
\]
The minimum is $\sum_i d_i$, achieved precisely when every $m_i=1$.
The minimum faithful module is unique up to a unitary intertwiner
preserving the labeled central blocks.  Moreover
\[
 \pi(\mathcal A)'=\bigoplus_i
  I_{d_i}\otimes M_{m_i}(\mathbb C),\qquad
 \pi(\mathcal A)'=Z(\pi(\mathcal A))
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad m_i=1\ \text{for all }i.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A full complex matrix algebra has, up to equivalence, one irreducible
unital representation, its defining module.  Restrict a faithful
representation to every central simple summand to obtain the displayed
multiplicities, which must all be positive.  Compute the commutant
block by block using matrix units.  The inequality and equality
criterion follow immediately.
\end{proof}

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

IIB-F074: Single-shot distinguishability and pure-state Euler invariant

Claim p2b:thm:v352-capacity-euler. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 3113–3142; original complete lines 3112–3141.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Single-shot distinguishability and pure-state Euler invariant]
\label{p2b:thm:v352-capacity-euler}
Let $C_1(\mathcal A)$ be the maximum number of algebraic states
perfectly discriminated by \emph{one} POVM with effects in
$\mathcal A$, and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal A)$ denote the abstract
pure-state space with its weak-$*$ topology.  Then
\[
 \boxed{C_1(\mathcal A)=\sum_i d_i
 =\chi(\mathcal P(\mathcal A))
 =\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H_{\min}},\qquad
 \mathcal P(\mathcal A)\simeq\bigsqcup_i\mathbb{CP}^{d_i-1}.
\]
Both quantities are independent of all faithful-representation
multiplicities $m_i$ as long as the \emph{same abstract effects}
constitute the test algebra.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A rank-one orthogonal basis of each summand, assembled across all
summands, gives $\sum_i d_i$ states and a single perfectly
discriminating POVM.  Conversely, for such a POVM
$\{e_j\}$ and perfectly discriminated density functionals
$\rho_j$, positivity implies that $e_j$ equals the identity on
the support of $\rho_j$ and vanishes on every other support.
The nonzero supports are pairwise orthogonal; their total rank is at
most $\sum_i d_i$.  A pure state of a finite direct sum belongs
to exactly one simple summand, whose pure states are rank-one
projectors $\mathbb{CP}^{d_i-1}$.  Finally
$\chi(\mathbb{CP}^{n})=n+1$ and the Euler characteristic is
additive over finite disjoint unions.  Apply the previous theorem.
\end{proof}

IIB-F075: Invariant fifteen-state capacity across the three algebra stages

Claim p2b:cor:v352-three-stage-capacity. Status VERIFIED-CONDITIONAL, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 3144–3170; original complete lines 3143–3169.

Current source object

\begin{corollary}[Invariant fifteen-state capacity across the three algebra stages]
\label{p2b:cor:v352-three-stage-capacity}
For the already generated abstract stages
\[
 \mathcal A_{\rm kin}=\mathbb C\oplus M_2\oplus M_2\oplus
 M_4\oplus M_3\oplus M_3,\quad
 \mathcal A_D=M_{11}\oplus M_4,\quad
 \mathcal A_{\rm full}=M_{15},
\]
\[
 \boxed{C_1(\mathcal A_{\rm kin})=C_1(\mathcal A_D)
  =C_1(\mathcal A_{\rm full})=15},\qquad
 \chi(\mathcal P(\mathcal A_j))=15.
\]
The algebra dimensions are $43,137,225$, the minimal-module
commutant dimensions are $6,2,1$, and the numbers of connected
pure-state components are $6,2,1$, respectively.  The maximum
single-shot classical alphabet carries $\log_2(15)$ bits of
\emph{distinguishability capacity}; this is not a physical bit rate.
The third algebra and its state/effect role remain conditional on
licensing the full field/event test domain.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Apply the preceding two theorems to the displayed block sizes.
The component count is the number of central simple summands, not
the Euler characteristic.
\end{proof}

IIB-F076: Normalized-copy no-go for universal multiplicity one

Claim p2b:prop:v352-normalized-amplification. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 3172–3195; original complete lines 3171–3194.

Current source object

\begin{proposition}[Normalized-copy no-go for universal multiplicity one]
\label{p2b:prop:v352-normalized-amplification}
For any $k\geq1$ and a finite $*$-polynomial $p$ in canonical
algebra elements $a_1,\ldots,a_n$,
\[
 \boxed{\frac{\operatorname{Tr}_{15k}
   p(a_1\otimes I_k,\ldots,a_n\otimes I_k)}{15k}
 =\frac{\operatorname{Tr}_{15}p(a_1,\ldots,a_n)}{15}.}
\]
The same algebraic effect statistics of a state are obtained by
partial trace over the unmarked multiplicity factor.  Thus normalized
trace words and these multiplicity-blind protocols cannot force
$k=1$.  A full GP3 whole-candidate comparison, independently
licensed multiplicity-resolving role, or absolute capacity witness
for an \emph{enlarged} algebra is still required to assert a
universally one-copy physical Hilbert carrier.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Polynomial evaluation commutes with tensoring by $I_k$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}(T\otimes I_k)=k\operatorname{Tr}(T)$.
For a density $\rho$ and effect $a\otimes I_k$, the partial-trace
identity is $\operatorname{Tr}[\rho(a\otimes I_k)]
=\operatorname{Tr}[(\operatorname{Tr}_k\rho)a]$.
\end{proof}

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

IIB-F078: Finite native-instrument histories descend under amplification

Claim p2b:thm:v353-multitime-amplification. Status VERIFIED-CONDITIONAL, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 3220–3250; original complete lines 3219–3247.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Finite native-instrument histories descend under amplification]
\label{p2b:thm:v353-multitime-amplification}
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-dimensional unital $C^*$-algebra and
$\pi_k(a)=\pi(a)\otimes I_k$ an unmarked common amplification of a
faithful finite-dimensional unital $*$-representation
$\pi:\mathcal A\to B(\mathcal H)$, with
$\pi(1_{\mathcal A})=I_{\mathcal H}$. For any finite sequence of completely
positive Heisenberg instrument branches
$\mathcal J_{s_j,x_j}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ with
$\sum_x\mathcal J_{s,x}(1)=1$, the joint probability of a history
in an initial density matrix $\rho$ is
\[
p(x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid s_1,\ldots,s_n)
=\omega_\rho\!\left(
\mathcal J_{s_1,x_1}\circ\cdots\circ
\mathcal J_{s_n,x_n}(1)\right),\quad
\omega_\rho(a)=\operatorname{Tr}[\rho\,\pi_k(a)].
\]
Every such history distribution agrees with that of a state on the
minimum faithful module of $\mathcal A$, independently of $k$;
the claim extends to classical-adaptive choices of settings.
This is a theorem about the abstract native instrument algebra, not about
all possible amplified-system apparatus interactions.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The specified composition takes values in $\mathcal A$, so all history
probabilities depend only on the restricted positive normalized functional
$\omega_\rho$. Every finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra state has a density
operator in its minimum faithful representation, proving equivalence for
all histories. Adaptivity only chooses a branch-dependent CP word.
\end{proof}

IIB-F079: Ancilla-stable native equivalence of all faithful multiplicities

Claim p2b:thm:v354-ancilla-stable-descent. Status VERIFIED-CONDITIONAL, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 3256–3279; original complete lines 3253–3276.

Current source object

\begin{theorem}[Ancilla-stable native equivalence of all faithful multiplicities]
\label{p2b:thm:v354-ancilla-stable-descent}
Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{\lambda}M_{d_\lambda}(\mathbb C)$.
Every finite-dimensional faithful unital $*$-representation has the form
$\pi_{\mathbf m}(a)=\bigoplus_\lambda(a_\lambda\otimes I_{m_\lambda})$
with $m_\lambda\ge1$. For any finite reference Hilbert space $\mathcal K$
and any density on the amplified representation tensored with
$\mathcal K$, sectorwise partial trace of the unmarked multiplicity
factors yields a canonical density reproducing all tests of
$\mathcal A\otimes B(\mathcal K)$. This equivalence persists through
all finite adaptive histories of CP instruments defined on that
abstract joint algebra. Therefore no such native protocol, even with
entangled finite ancillas, can infer $\mathbf m$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Decompose the state by central sectors and trace out each
$\mathbb C^{m_\lambda}$. The resulting canonical block density gives
identical expectations for every abstract joint observable.
Each $\pi_{\mathbf m}\otimes\operatorname{id}_{M_n}$ is a
complete-order isomorphism onto its image. Composing CP Heisenberg
instrument maps in the abstract algebra preserves the equality
on each outcome-history branch. No operation outside the native algebra
is included.
\end{proof}

IIB-F080: GP3 and physical-operation boundary

Claim p2b:rem:v355-native-operation-firewall. Status VERIFIED, lifecycle ACTIVE. Current source lines 3284–3294; original complete lines 3281–3291.

Current source object

\begin{remark}[GP3 and physical-operation boundary]
\label{p2b:rem:v355-native-operation-firewall}
The canonical minimum faithful representation determines the complete
operator-algebraic native test capacity, but neither the actual microscopic
Hilbert-space multiplicities nor whether a multiplicity-sensitive operation
occurs. These theorems do not remove GP3 as a primitive principle or replace
its universal whole-candidate comparison certificate. Finite entangled
ancillas change none of the abstract-native statistics, even though an
independently licensed commutant-sensitive channel would change the test
algebra and invalidate that no-go's premises.
\end{remark}

The complete object is byte-identical to its audited v2.135 counterpart.

{

    "lines": [
      1647,
      1666
    ],
    "source_excerpt": "\\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic first-coordinate sector and exact orbit-retention criterion]\n\\label{p2:thm:intrinsic-coordinate-sector}\nOn the generated round \\(S^3(\\Rmom)\\), the first nonconstant scalar\nLaplace eigenspace is the intrinsically defined four-dimensional\n\\(\\Spin(4)\\)-irreducible object\n\\[\n E_1\\cong V_{\\frac12,\\frac12},\\qquad\n \\lambda_1=\\frac3{\\Rmom^2}.\n\\]\nIf a finite reciprocal role has a frozen \\emph{object-typed} coordinate\nport with nonzero image of \\(E_1\\), and that port is faithful and\nclosed under the full inherited \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-action and linear\nobject operations, then it must retain the entire one-copy image of\n\\(E_1\\).  It cannot retain just one axis or a proper nonzero part of\nthat irreducible object.  A scalar readout without the coordinate-object\nport, or a role inheriting only a proper symmetry subgroup, does not by\nitself imply this full-sector retention.  This statement determines\nirreducible \\emph{type support}, not unmarked multiplicity in a larger\nrealization or an independently prepared coordinate basis.\n\\end{theorem}"
  },

{
  "id": "BH-IIB-A-B2-MULT-UNMARKED-001",
  "normalized_statement": "On the specified irreducible factor V tensor M with dim M>1, frozen multiplicity-slot data have every I_V tensor U, U in U(M), as a symmetry and no distinguished multiplicity line/subspace/label. This says nothing about all other complete-candidate data.",

      1222,

    ],
    "source_excerpt": "\\begin{proposition}[Unmarked multiplicity does not supply a canonical copy selector]\n\\label{p2b:prop:v279-no-canonical-copy-selector}\nLet \\(V\\ne0\\) be an irreducible \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-module and let\n\\(M\\cong\\mathbb C^m\\) with \\(m>1\\). Suppose the frozen structure on\n\\(V\\otimes M\\) carries no distinguished line, subspace, or multiplicity\nlabel, so every \\(I_V\\otimes U\\) for \\(U\\in U(M)\\) is a symmetry of the\n\\emph{multiplicity-slot data}.  Then no one-dimensional complex subspace\nof \\(M\\) is invariant under all these symmetries, and there is no\nnonzero \\(U(M)\\)-invariant linear functional \\(M\\to\\mathbb C\\) (with\ntrivial target action).  In particular a projector choosing a single\ncopy \\(V\\otimes\\mathbb C\\subset V\\otimes M\\), or a nonzero linear\nretraction to such an unmarked copy, is not canonically generated\nfrom the multiplicity-slot data alone."

    "source_excerpt": "\\begin{corollary}[Invariant preparations for the native operation algebras]\n\\label{p2b:cor:v233-native-invariant-states}\nFor the mixed scalar-position/enriched-momentum carrier\n\\(\\mathcal P_m\\otimes\\mathcal H_1\\), let the represented algebra be\ngenerated by the factor actions and all native nonzero coordinate\nedges. With \\(d_m=\\dim\\mathcal P_m\\), its full block algebra is\n\\(M_{11d_m}\\oplus M_{4d_m}\\).\nThe densities invariant under all of its unitary conjugations are\nexactly\n\\[\n \\rho_p=\\frac{p}{11d_m}P_{\\rm geo}\n       +\\frac{1-p}{4d_m}P_{\\rm sp},\\qquad 0\\le p\\le1.\n\\]\nOn the matched enriched product with Born exchange, the algebra is\n\\(M_{121}\\oplus M_{88}\\oplus M_{16}\\), and these densities are\n\\[\n \\rho_{a,b,c}=\\frac a{121}P_{gg}\n       +\\frac b{88}(P_{gs}+P_{sg})+\\frac c{16}P_{ss},\n \\qquad a,b,c\\ge0,\\quad a+b+c=1.\n\\]\nThe normalized full traces have \\(p=11/15\\) and\n\\((a,b,c)=(121,88,16)/225\\), respectively; the stated operation\ninvariances do not select those points."
  },

Corollary~\\ref{p1:cor:level-one-coordinate-completion-moduli}\nproves that, after quotienting by sector rephasings, the four-edge forest\nleaves exactly three nonnegative reduced magnitudes:\n\\[\n \\mathfrak M_{\\rm coord}(\\mathcal H_1)/{\\sim}\n \\;\\cong\\;\n \\mathbb R_{\\ge0}^{3},\n \\qquad\n [\\mathsf C]\\longleftrightarrow\n (r_{1,0},r_{0,1},\\varrho_{\\rm sp}).\n\\]\nHere the first two entries are the two geometric off-diagonal magnitudes and\n\\(\\varrho_{\\rm sp}\\) is the phase-invariant protected magnitude. BH-IIB-A-B3-CSTAR-15-137-001

{
  "id": "BH-IIB-A-B3-CSTAR-15-137-001",
  "normalized_statement": "A is a UNITAL finite-dimensional complex C*-SUBALGEBRA faithfully included in M15(C), with complex algebra dimension exactly137. The represented Hilbert dimension is exactly15.",
  "category": "DOMAIN",
  "type": "EXACT SOURCE-SCOPED CONDITION",
  "epistemic_status": "STIPULATED",
  "lifecycle": "ACTIVE",
  "first_occurrence": {
    "paper": "Paper2B",
    "file": "Paper2B-MomentumCarrier-v2_135.tex",
    "lines": [
      2639,
      2658
    ],
    "source_excerpt": "\\begin{theorem}[Reverse rigidity of the native $15/137$ data]\n\\label{p2b:thm:v264-algebra-rigidity}\nIf $\\mathcal A\\subseteq M_{15}(\\CC)$ is a \\emph{unital complex\nfinite-dimensional $C^*$-subalgebra} with\n$\\dim_{\\CC}\\mathcal A=137$, then its represented form is, up to a\nunitary change of basis,\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\mathcal A=M_{11}(\\CC)\\oplus M_4(\\CC)}\n\\]\nwith each simple block represented once.  Neither the original\ncoordinate-graph constructor nor its occurring action/readout ownership\nfollows from these two numbers alone.\n\\end{theorem}\n\\begin{proof}\nWrite the faithful unital representation as\n$\\mathcal A\\cong\\bigoplus_i M_{n_i}(\\CC)$ on\n$\\bigoplus_i(\\CC^{n_i}\\otimes\\CC^{m_i})$, where $m_i\\ge1$.\nThen $\\sum_i n_i^2=137$ and $\\sum_i n_im_i=15$.\nIf every $n_i\\le9$, then\n$137=\\sum_i n_i^2\\le9\\sum_i n_i\\le135$, impossible."
  },
  "first_occurrence_priority": "FIRST-KNOWN exact typed predicate in currently checked logical dependency ancestry; not absolute global priority claim.",
  "canonical_aliases": [],
  "proved_or_discharged_by": [],
  "direct_prerequisites": [],

  "deduplication_check": "Compared 177 active canonical conditions. Differently typed generic operator/physical-word/coordinate-occurrence predicates are not silently equated.",
  "quantifiers": "All such represented C* algebras; an arbitrary137-dimensional linear space or abstract algebra without faithful15-dimensional unital representation is outside scope."
}

Its sphere topology and rank-one geometry are the II-A results\nin Theorems~\\ref{p2:thm:rank-one-topology-spin} and\n\\ref{p2:thm:rank-one-space-form-einstein}.  From\nthis point onward, \\emph{momentum space} means\n\\[\n        M_p\\cong S^3_A(\\Rmom)\\cong SU(2).\n\\]\nThe circle \\(S^1_A\\cong U(1)\\) is exported as the compact scalar succession\nparent but is not part of the Paper-II momentum construction.  The round\nmetric, its \\(SO(4)\\) isometry group, and the lifted \\(\\Spin(4)\\) symmetry are\nconsequences of the derived \\(SU(2)\\) branch.\nThe compatible Hopf fibrations form a conjugacy class with no preferred\nmember; one left/common-phase Hopf/contact representative and its normalization\nare now fixed from the Paper-I-A atlas. BND-IIB-B1-DESCENT-001

{
  "id": "BND-IIB-B1-DESCENT-001",
  "title": "Spin4 integration and SO4 operator descent",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2B-MomentumCarrier-v2_135.tex",
    "lines": [
      434,
      488
    ],
    "source_excerpt": "\\begin{proposition}[Finite sector grammar and the exact descent boundary]\n\\label{p2:prop:algebra-sector-grammar}\nLet a GP1-finite, GP2-host-faithful complex Hilbert realization of the momentum\nhost carry the derived connected isometry symmetry of\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:single-su2-derived-spin4-isometries}.  The resulting\nfinite-dimensional unitary representation integrates to the universal lift\n\\(\\Spin(4)\\), and its irreducible complex sectors are, up to unitary\nequivalence,\n\\[\n V_{j_L}\\otimes V_{j_R},\n \\qquad\n (j_L,j_R)\\in\n \\tfrac12\\ZZ_{\\ge0}\\times\\tfrac12\\ZZ_{\\ge0}.\n\\]\nEvery such Lie-algebra representation integrates uniquely to the simply\nconnected derived symmetry group\n\\(\\Spin(4)=SU(2)_L\\times SU(2)_R\\).  This integration introduces neither a\nsecond momentum parent nor a choice of deck data on \\(M_p\\).\n\nLet \\(z=(-1,-1)\\) be the kernel of\n\\(\\Spin(4)\\to SO(4)\\).  On \\(V_{j_L}\\otimes V_{j_R}\\),\n\\[\n \\pi_{j_L,j_R}(z)\n =\n (-1)^{2(j_L+j_R)}\\mathbf1.\n\\]\nConsequently conjugation on the endomorphisms of any single irreducible sector\ndescends to \\(SO(4)\\).  On a direct sum of sectors, conjugation on an\ninter-sector block descends precisely when its source and target have the same\ncentral character.  The generated operator doctrine used in this paper is\nwithin that descent domain: Killing generators and equivariant projectors are\nblock diagonal, while the coordinate type\n\\((\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\) changes \\(j_L+j_R\\) by an integer and therefore\npreserves the central character.  No descent statement is made for arbitrary\nendomorphisms mixing the two central-character classes.\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nFinite-dimensional unitary representations of a compact semisimple Lie\nalgebra are completely reducible\n\\cite{fulton1991representation,Hall2015lie}.  The irreducibles of a direct sum\nare outer tensor products of irreducibles of its two factors, and the\nirreducibles of \\(\\mathfrak{su}(2)\\) are indexed by\n\\(j\\in\\tfrac12\\ZZ_{\\ge0}\\) \\cite{fulton1991representation}.  Lie's\nintegration theorem \\cite{Hall2015lie} gives a unique\nrepresentation of the simply connected group \\(\\Spin(4)\\).\n\nThe central element \\(-1\\in SU(2)\\) acts on \\(V_j\\) by\n\\((-1)^{2j}\\), giving the displayed central character.  On\n\\(\\operatorname{Hom}(V_\\lambda,V_\\mu)\\), conjugation by \\(z\\) is the quotient\nof the two central characters, so it is trivial exactly when they agree.\nFinally, a coordinate channel has\n\\((\\Delta j_L,\\Delta j_R)=(\\pm\\tfrac12,\\pm\\tfrac12)\\), hence changes\n\\(j_L+j_R\\) by \\(0\\) or \\(\\pm1\\).  This proves the stated descent boundary.\n\\end{proof}"
  },

{

  "title": "Representation word degree is classification",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2B-MomentumCarrier-v2_135.tex",
    "lines": [
      666,
      760
    ],
    "source_excerpt": "\\subsubsection{Intrinsic spinor seed, canonical host images, and intrinsic word length}\n\\label{p2:subsec:constructor-grammar-word-length}\n\nLet \\(S_+\\) and \\(S_-\\) denote the two intrinsic \\(k=0\\) chiral\nDirac/Killing-spinor spaces of the round host, and put\n\\[\n F_L:=S_+,\\qquad F_R:=S_-,\\qquad S:=S_+\\oplus S_-.\n\\]\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Canonical lowest spinor seed and weight classification]\n\\label{p2b:thm:seed-atomicity}\nFor the round momentum parent and its derived universal lift \\(\\Spin(4)\\), the\nintrinsic lowest two chiral Dirac/Killing-spinor spaces supplied by the round\nspin geometry satisfy\n\\[\n \\boxed{S_+\\cong V_{\\frac12,0},\\qquad S_-\\cong V_{0,\\frac12}.}\n\\]\nTheir direct sum \\(S=S_+\\oplus S_-\\) is faithful and the unordered pair is\nstable under factor interchange.  After this geometric generation, their\nhighest weights are the two fundamental weights \\(\\omega_L,\\omega_R\\), which\nare the atoms of the mathematical dominant-weight monoid\n\\[\n P^+(\\Spin(4))\\cong\\mathbb Z_{\\ge0}\\omega_L\\oplus\n \\mathbb Z_{\\ge0}\\omega_R.\n\\]\nThis last statement classifies the already generated spinor seed; it does not\nidentify the physical construction monoid with the whole dominant-weight\nmonoid and is not the selector of \\(S_\\pm\\).\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe \\(k=0\\) cases of the Paper-I-A spinor harmonic theorem give the two intrinsic\nlowest chiral spaces and their \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-types.  The center of one factor\nacts nontrivially on one chiral module and trivially on the other, so the\nkernels of the two factor actions intersect trivially and \\(S\\) is faithful.\nFactor interchange exchanges the two chiral spaces.  The final dominant-weight\nstatement is the standard classification of irreducible\n\\(SU(2)_L\\times SU(2)_R\\)-modules and is used here only after the geometric\nobjects have been generated.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Word monoid versus physical constructor monoid]\n\\label{p2b:rem:seed-semantic-revision}\nFor representation-theoretic bookkeeping define the free word monoid\n\\[\n M_{\\rm word}:=\\mathbb N[F_L]\\oplus\\mathbb N[F_R].\n\\]\nIt records tensor-word length built from the already generated spinor seed.\nIt is not asserted to equal the GP2 physical construction monoid of the\nmomentum host.  In particular, the former non-atomic seed countermodels remain\nuseful diagnostics of weaker generation-based definitions, but they do not\ncompete with the geometrically fixed lowest spinor spaces above.  Their\ndetailed comparison is deferred to Paper~II-F, Section~\\ref{p2b:app:legacy-selector}.\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Minimal tensor-word length]\n\\label{p2b:lem:minimal-word-length}\nFor an irreducible \\(V_{j_L,j_R}\\), define the representation-theoretic word\nlength\n\\[\n \\ell(V_{j_L,j_R})\n :=\\min\\{r\\ge0:V_{j_L,j_R}\\prec(F_L\\oplus F_R)^{\\otimes r}\\}.\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\ell(V_{j_L,j_R})=2j_L+2j_R.}\n\\]\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nA word with \\(r_L\\) left and \\(r_R\\) right fundamentals has every constituent\nsatisfying \\(j_L\\le r_L/2\\) and \\(j_R\\le r_R/2\\), so\n\\(r\\ge2j_L+2j_R\\).  Conversely, \\(V_{j_L}\\) occurs as the highest-spin\nconstituent of \\((V_{1/2})^{\\otimes2j_L}\\), and similarly on the right.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{corollary}[Intrinsic word length and half-level normalization]\n\\label{p2b:cor:word-degree-derived}\nThe half-level convention is the derived representation label\n\\[\n m(V_{j_L,j_R})=\\frac12\\ell(V_{j_L,j_R})=j_L+j_R.\n\\]\nAt fixed integer word length \\(N\\), the multiplicity-free shell and cumulative\nprefix have dimensions\n\\[\n \\binom{N+3}{3},\\qquad \\binom{N+4}{4},\n\\]\nrespectively.  This is classification data; it does not make unrestricted\ntensor powers physical GP2-generated content.\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe length identity is Lemma~\\ref{p2b:lem:minimal-word-length}.  At fixed\n\\(N=a+b\\), sum \\((a+1)(b+1)\\) over \\(a+b=N\\), then sum the shells.\n\\end{proof}"
  },

{
  "id": "BND-IIB-B1-IMAGE-001",
  "title": "Finite section-object image and same-role inheritance",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2B-MomentumCarrier-v2_135.tex",
    "lines": [
      763,
      1110
    ],
    "source_excerpt": "\\label{p2b:subsec:unconditional-momentum-host}\n\nPaper~II-A freezes the initial momentum-seed dependency frontier in\nDefinition~\\ref{p2:def:momentum-seed-frontier}.  This paper verifies its\nround-host provenance.  Let \\(E_k\\) denote the scalar harmonic level \\(k\\) of\nthe round parent.  By the Paper-I-A representation-harmonic package,\n\\[\n E_0\\cong(0,0),\\qquad E_1\\cong(\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12),\n\\]\nand the intrinsic lowest two spinor objects are\n\\(S_+\\cong(\\tfrac12,0)\\) and \\(S_-\\cong(0,\\tfrac12)\\).  The round gradient and\nthe vector-field Lie bracket are host-natural constructors available before\nany finite representation level is chosen.  By Paper~II-A's parent-geometric\nobject typing, \\(\\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj}\\) is the tangent-section object\nsort of the same momentum parent, whereas the induced derivation action is a\ndistinct operation-typed output co-realized by the same licensed constructor\nword.  No tensor-word boundary,\ncompression map, component ceiling, or pointwise scalar multiplication as a\nfinite carrier constructor belongs to this seed frontier.\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Canonical bracket linearization and bivector--Killing bridge]\n\\label{p2b:lem:canonical-bracket-image}\nIdentify the real first harmonic space \\(E_1^{\\mathbb R}\\) with the ambient\nvector space \\(\\mathbb R^4\\) by\n\\[\n u\\longmapsto f_u,\\qquad f_u(x):=\\langle u,x\\rangle,\n \\qquad x\\in S^3(\\Rmom).\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n \\nabla f_u=u-\\frac{f_u}{\\Rmom^2}x\n\\]\nand\n\\[\n [\\nabla f_u,\\nabla f_v]\n =\\frac1{\\Rmom^2}\\bigl(f_u v-f_v u\\bigr).\n\\]\nThus the constituted bilinear constructor\n\\[\n \\beta:E_1^{\\mathbb R}\\times E_1^{\\mathbb R}\n \\longrightarrow\\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj},\\qquad\n \\beta(f_u,f_v):=[\\nabla f_u,\\nabla f_v],\n\\]\nhas a canonical real linear hull.  Because \\(\\beta\\) is alternating, its\nunique mathematical linearization is\n\\[\n \\bar\\beta:\\Lambda^2E_1^{\\mathbb R}\n \\longrightarrow\\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj},\n \\qquad\n \\bar\\beta(u\\wedge v):=[\\nabla f_u,\\nabla f_v].\n\\]\nIt satisfies\n\\[\n Z_\\beta:=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\operatorname{im}\\beta\n =\\operatorname{im}\\bar\\beta\n =\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}.\n\\]\nEquivalently,\n\\[\n \\Theta:=\\Rmom^2\\bar\\beta:\n \\Lambda^2E_1^{\\mathbb R}\\longrightarrow\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill},\n \\qquad\n \\Theta(u\\wedge v):=\\Rmom^2[\\nabla f_u,\\nabla f_v]\n\\]\nis a canonical \\(SO(4)\\)-equivariant isomorphism onto the six-dimensional\nKilling-field module.  After complexification,\n\\[\n (\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill})_{\\mathbb C}\n \\cong\\Lambda^2_{\\mathbb C}\n \\cong(1,0)\\oplus(0,1).\n\\]\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe displayed gradient is the orthogonal projection of the constant ambient\nvector \\(u\\) to \\(T_xS^3\\).  Differentiating it in the ambient space and\nantisymmetrizing gives the bracket formula.  The vector field\n\\[\n x\\longmapsto\\langle u,x\\rangle v-\\langle v,x\\rangle u\n\\]\nis the infinitesimal rotation associated with the ambient bivector\n\\(u\\wedge v\\).  The standard map \\(\\Lambda^2\\mathbb R^4\\to\\mathfrak{so}(4)\\)\nis an isomorphism, so \\(\\Theta\\), and hence \\(\\bar\\beta\\), is injective and\nhas image all of \\(\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}\\).  Since the image of the induced\nlinear map is exactly the real span of the outputs of the original bilinear\nmap, this proves the displayed identity for \\(Z_\\beta\\).  Naturality of the\nambient inner product makes \\(\\Theta\\) equivariant.  The Paper-I-A\nquadratic-shell theorem gives the same linear-image identity and the displayed\n\\(\\Spin(4)\\)-type.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Canonical normalized first-harmonic gradient port]\n\\label{p2b:lem:gradient-port}\nOn the round host, the gradient is a natural, \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-equivariant\nisomorphism of object modules\n\\[\n \\nabla:E_1\\xrightarrow{\\ \\sim\\ }\\nabla E_1\n \\subset\\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj}.\n\\]\nFor the round \\(L^2\\) scalar and vector-field inner products,\n\\[\n \\langle\\nabla f,\\nabla g\\rangle_{L^2}\n =\\frac3{\\Rmom^2}\\langle f,g\\rangle_{L^2},\\qquad\n U_\\nabla:=\\frac{\\Rmom}{\\sqrt3}\\nabla,\n \\qquad U_\\nabla^{-1}=-\\frac{\\Rmom}{\\sqrt3}\\operatorname{div}\n \\quad\\text{on }\\nabla E_1.\n\\]\nThis unitary object-port map identifies the two isomorphic four-dimensional\nrepresentations inside a one-copy presentation.  Their source/target roles\nremain distinct; it does not identify a section object with an induced\noperation occurrence or add a physical gradient-evaluation constructor.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\begin{proof}\nEvery \\(f\\in E_1\\) satisfies\n\\(-\\Delta f=3f/\\Rmom^2\\).  Integration by parts on the compact round\nsphere gives the inner-product identity and the displayed inverse.\nThe metric and Laplacian commute with the derived \\(\\Spin(4)\\) action,\nso the map is equivariant and independent of a chosen basis.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Conformal-field Lie closure, in the smooth host]\n\\label{p2b:prop:conformal-host-closure}\nFor \\(u,v\\in\\mathbb R^4\\) put \\(G_u:=\\nabla f_u\\), and for\n\\(A\\in\\mathfrak{so}(4)\\) put \\(K_A(x):=Ax\\).  Their ordinary\nvector-field brackets obey\n\\[\n [G_u,G_v]=K_{(vu^\\top-uv^\\top)/\\Rmom^2},\\quad\n [K_A,G_u]=-G_{Au},\\quad\n [K_A,K_B]=K_{BA-AB}.\n\\]\nConsequently\n\\(\\mathfrak c:=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\{G_u,K_A\\}\\)\nis a ten-dimensional Lie algebra isomorphic to \\(\\mathfrak{so}(4,1)\\).\nAs a representation of the \\emph{compact} derived \\(\\Spin(4)\\),\n\\[\n \\mathfrak c_{\\mathbb C}\n \\cong(\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\oplus(1,0)\\oplus(0,1)\n \\cong\\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_+\\oplus S_-),\n \\qquad \\mathcal H_1\\cong\\mathbf1\\oplus S\\oplus\\mathfrak c_{\\mathbb C}.\n\\]\nThus \\(15=1+4+10\\) is an intrinsic host-classification of the\nalready generated six types.  Neither \\(\\mathfrak{so}(4,1)\\) nor\nits noncompact finite-dimensional action is introduced as a new physical\nmomentum group or a faithful unitary finite-carrier operation constructor.\n\\end{proposition}\n\\begin{proof}\nThe first bracket is Lemma~\\ref{p2b:lem:canonical-bracket-image}.\nDirect differentiation of \\(K_A\\) and \\(G_u\\) gives the other two.\nThe injective map\n\\[\n K_A\\longmapsto\\begin{pmatrix}-A&0\\\\0&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad\n G_u\\longmapsto\\begin{pmatrix}0&u/\\Rmom\\\\u^\\top/\\Rmom&0\\end{pmatrix}\n\\]\npreserves the three brackets, and its image is the standard\n\\(\\mathfrak{so}(4,1)\\) block presentation.  The four gradients have\n\\((\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\)-type; the six Killing fields decompose as\n\\((1,0)\\oplus(0,1)\\).  Expanding the symmetric square of the two\nchiral defining modules proves the final representation identity.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Coordinate-algebra blocks versus geometric type blocks]\n\\label{p2b:rem:conformal-block-compatibility}\nThe geometric decomposition\n\\(\\mathbf1\\oplus\\mathfrak c_{\\mathbb C}\\oplus S\\)\norganizes \\(\\mathcal H_1\\) into dimensions \\(11+4\\).\nWhere the separately constituted intrinsic coordinate tuple and its\ncompletion hypotheses produce\n\\(\\mathcal A_D\\cong M_{11}(\\mathbb C)\\oplus M_4(\\mathbb C)\\),\nthose block sizes agree with the geometric organization.  Matrix\nsimplicity and the dimension \\(137=11^2+4^2\\) depend on the separate\ncoordinate-intertwiner/word calculation, not on the decomposition\n\\(11+4\\) alone, and do not select a physical operation or state.\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Maximal exact unital scalar derivation subalgebra]\n\\label{p2b:prop:maximal-finite-scalar-action}\nSet \\(\\mathcal P_1:=E_0\\oplus E_1\\subset C^\\infty(S^3(\\Rmom))\\).\nFor a smooth-host field \\(X\\in\\mathfrak c\\), let\n\\(\\delta_X(h)=X(h)\\) be its \\emph{ordinary} scalar derivation.  Then\n\\[\n \\delta_X(\\mathcal P_1)\\subseteq\\mathcal P_1\n \\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad X\\in\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}.\n\\]\nThis is the maximal exact action \\emph{among fields in}\n\\(\\mathfrak c\\), conditional only on taking \\(\\mathcal P_1\\) as the\nspecified scalar-operation target; the proposition does not assert that\nthe physical operation grammar has selected that target.\n\\end{proposition}\n\\begin{proof}\nWrite \\(X=K_A+G_u\\).  A Killing field preserves \\(E_0\\) and\n\\(E_1\\), since \\(K_A(f_v)=-f_{Av}\\).\nOn the other hand,\n\\[\n G_u(f_v)=u\\cdot v-\\frac{f_uf_v}{\\Rmom^2}.\n\\]\nIf \\(u\\ne0\\), take \\(v=u\\).  The traceless quadratic harmonic part of\n\\(f_u^2\\) is nonzero; the Killing term has degree one and cannot\ncancel it.  Thus \\(X\\) fails to preserve \\(\\mathcal P_1\\).\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Conditional infinite tower under retained gradient evaluation]\n\\label{p2b:prop:gradient-evaluation-no-go}\nConsider a \\emph{different, enlarged} physical grammar that (i) licenses\nordinary scalar evaluation by \\(G=\\nabla f\\), \\(f=x_1\\),\n(ii) retains each output in a scalar carrier sort, and (iii) licenses\nrepeated evaluation on those outputs.  Its scalar carrier closure is\ninfinite-dimensional.\n\\end{proposition}\n\\begin{proof}\nLet \\(F_0=f\\), \\(F_{n+1}=G(F_n)\\).  On functions of \\(f\\),\n\\(G=(1-f^2/\\Rmom^2)d/df\\).  Inductively \\(F_n\\) has degree\n\\(n+1\\) with leading coefficient\n\\((-1)^n n!/\\Rmom^{2n}\\ne0\\).  Therefore the\n\\(F_n\\) are linearly independent as functions on the sphere.  This\nis an obstruction only to the explicitly enlarged retention/reuse grammar,\nnot to the frozen Paper-II-A momentum seed.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Typed constructor and evaluation boundary]\n\\label{p2b:rem:typed-momentum-operation-grammar}\nThe frozen seed licenses the \\emph{object} words\n\\(E_1\\xrightarrow{\\nabla}\\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj}\\) and\n\\(E_1\\times E_1\\xrightarrow{\\beta}\\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj}\\),\nwith section-object linear-span retention for \\(Z_\\beta\\).  An induced\noperation \\(K\\mapsto\\delta_K\\) remains a distinct port and is physically\nco-realized only on the action target and evaluations explicitly licensed by\nthe parent constructor signature.  Neither ambient pointwise multiplication,\nnor arbitrary \\(G(h)\\), nor reuse of a scalar evaluation output as a new\nfinite-carrier seed follows from these object words.  The host Lie closure\nof Proposition~\\ref{p2b:prop:conformal-host-closure} is a mathematical\nclassification, not a recursive enlargement of the physical constructor\nsignature.  A conformal-density Lie derivative would change the typed\noperation and is not silently substituted for \\(\\delta_X\\).\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Literal bilinear image versus generated linear image]\n\\label{p2b:rem:beta-set-image-linear-hull}\nThe literal set image \\(\\operatorname{im}\\beta\\) consists of fields\ncorresponding to decomposable bivectors \\(u\\wedge v\\) and is a proper subset\nof \\(\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}\\).  For example,\n\\(e_1\\wedge e_2+e_3\\wedge e_4\\) is not decomposable because its exterior\nsquare is nonzero.  No equality\n\\(\\operatorname{im}\\beta=\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}\\) is claimed.  The\nsix-dimensional object used below is the generated real linear subspace\n\\(Z_\\beta=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\operatorname{im}\\beta\\).\n\\end{remark}\n\n% BEGIN FRAMEWORK v2.264: LITERAL TWO-BRACKET CONVERSE\n\\begin{lemma}[Sharp literal two-bracket realization of every round Killing section]\n\\label{p2b:lem:v264-two-bracket-surjection}\nOn the declared round momentum host, with the \\emph{already constituted}\naddition in the real vector-space section-object target, the composite\n\\[\n \\mathfrak B:(E_1^{\\mathbb R})^4\\longrightarrow\n \\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj},\\qquad\n \\mathfrak B(f,g,h,k)=[\\nabla f,\\nabla g]+[\\nabla h,\\nabla k]\n\\]\nhas literal set image precisely $\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}$.  Under the\nisomorphism $\\Theta:\\Lambda^2E_1^{\\mathbb R}\\to\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}$\nof Lemma~\\ref{p2b:lem:canonical-bracket-image}, a Killing section\n$\\Theta(A)$ belongs to the \\emph{single}-bracket set image exactly when\n\\[\n A\\wedge A=0,\n \\quad\\text{equivalently}\\quad\n \\|A_+\\|=\\|A_-\\|\n\\]\nfor the self-dual/anti-self-dual decomposition of real two-forms.\nThe bound of two brackets is sharp.  This uses only finite composition\nand addition in the frozen target object sort; $\\Lambda^2E_1$ is a\n\\emph{classification} device, not a newly physicalized constructor.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\begin{proof}\nEvery real alternating $4\\times4$ matrix admits an orthonormal skew\nnormal form $A=\\lambda e_1\\wedge e_2+\\mu e_3\\wedge e_4$.\nSince $u\\mapsto f_u$ is real linear, each coefficient can be absorbed\ninto one harmonic argument, so $\\Theta(A)$ is the sum of two bracket\noutputs. Conversely each such sum is Killing by the preceding lemma.\nA nonzero real bivector in dimension four is decomposable if and only if\n$A\\wedge A=0$ (the vanishing Pfaffian criterion). As\n$A\\wedge A=(\\|A_+\\|^2-\\|A_-\\|^2)\\operatorname{vol}$ with the same\nHodge normalization on the two halves, the norm criterion is equivalent.\nThe form $e_1\\wedge e_2+e_3\\wedge e_4$ is not decomposable, proving\nthat one bracket cannot always suffice.\n\\end{proof}\n\\begin{remark}[Finite-image inheritance without a span/image ambiguity]\n\\label{p2b:rem:v264-literal-inheritance}\nThe preceding literal surjection makes the premise of\nLemma~\\ref{p2:lem:gp2-finite-generated-image-inheritance} directly\napplicable to $\\operatorname{im}\\mathfrak B$ whenever the previously\nfrozen vector-space section-object addition is consumed. It strengthens\nCorollary~\\ref{p2b:cor:bracket-image-same-carrier}; it does not infer\nthat addition is physical merely from a computed image and does not\nsupply the distinct GP3 whole-candidate comparison certificate.\n\\end{remark}\n% END FRAMEWORK v2.264: LITERAL TWO-BRACKET CONVERSE\n\n\\begin{corollary}[Inherited same-role typing of the canonical bracket linear image]\n\\label{p2b:cor:bracket-image-same-carrier}\nThe finite-dimensional real section-object subspace\n\\[\n Z_\\beta\n =\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\operatorname{im}\\beta\n =\\operatorname{im}\\bar\\beta\n =\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}\n\\]\nbelongs to the momentum role's generated object closure.  Its complexification\n\\((Z_\\beta)_{\\mathbb C}=(\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill})_{\\mathbb C}\\) belongs to the\nmomentum carrier.  The corresponding infinitesimal Killing action remains\na distinct operation-typed node and is co-realized, not independently\nactualized.\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe constituted composite\n\\[\n \\beta:E_1^{\\mathbb R}\\times E_1^{\\mathbb R}\n \\longrightarrow\\Gamma(TS^3)_{\\rm sec,obj}\n\\]\nlands in the same-role parent geometric object sort fixed by Paper~II-A.\nThat target sort is a real vector-space object sort, so its already\nconstituted addition and scalar multiplication force every generated object\nsubspace containing all \\(\\beta\\)-outputs to contain their real linear hull\n\\(Z_\\beta\\).  This is closure within the target's object typing; it neither\nconstitutes \\(\\Lambda^2E_1^{\\mathbb R}\\) as a new physical constructor nor\nadds arbitrary tensor or polynomial closure.\n\nBy Lemma~\\ref{p2b:lem:canonical-bracket-image}, the resulting linear image\n\\(Z_\\beta=\\operatorname{im}\\bar\\beta=\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}\\) is\nfinite-dimensional, candidate-independent, intrinsically characterized,\nnonredundant, invariant, and carries the induced \\(\\Spin(4)\\) transformation\nlaw.  Paper~II-A's constructor-relative generated closure and finite\ngenerated-image inheritance\nLemma~\\ref{p2:lem:gp2-finite-generated-image-inheritance} therefore preserve\nthe section-object typing of \\(Z_\\beta\\); retaining only its induced\nderivation/Killing-operation occurrence would violate GP2 typed host\nfaithfulness and no-omission.\n\nThe frozen frontier generates no autonomous role label, separate carrier,\ncross-role variance, or separating test that would split this inherited\nlinear object image from the momentum role.  Paper~II-A's same-role\nno-splitting Lemma~\\ref{p2:lem:gp2-same-role-no-splitting} therefore places\nits finite-dimensional object copy, after complexification, in the momentum\ncarrier.  GP2 sort faithfulness keeps the induced operation occurrence\nseparate.  The conclusion objectifies only this canonical generated linear\nsubspace, not the ambient infinite-dimensional section space\n\\(\\Gamma(TS^3)\\).\n\\end{proof}"

BND-IIB-B1-CONFORMAL-001

{
  "id": "BND-IIB-B1-CONFORMAL-001",
  "title": "Host conformal algebra and fixed scalar action target",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2B-MomentumCarrier-v2_135.tex",
    "lines": [
      884,
      962
    ],
    "source_excerpt": "\\begin{proposition}[Conformal-field Lie closure, in the smooth host]\n\\label{p2b:prop:conformal-host-closure}\nFor \\(u,v\\in\\mathbb R^4\\) put \\(G_u:=\\nabla f_u\\), and for\n\\(A\\in\\mathfrak{so}(4)\\) put \\(K_A(x):=Ax\\).  Their ordinary\nvector-field brackets obey\n\\[\n [G_u,G_v]=K_{(vu^\\top-uv^\\top)/\\Rmom^2},\\quad\n [K_A,G_u]=-G_{Au},\\quad\n [K_A,K_B]=K_{BA-AB}.\n\\]\nConsequently\n\\(\\mathfrak c:=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\{G_u,K_A\\}\\)\nis a ten-dimensional Lie algebra isomorphic to \\(\\mathfrak{so}(4,1)\\).\nAs a representation of the \\emph{compact} derived \\(\\Spin(4)\\),\n\\[\n \\mathfrak c_{\\mathbb C}\n \\cong(\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\oplus(1,0)\\oplus(0,1)\n \\cong\\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_+\\oplus S_-),\n \\qquad \\mathcal H_1\\cong\\mathbf1\\oplus S\\oplus\\mathfrak c_{\\mathbb C}.\n\\]\nThus \\(15=1+4+10\\) is an intrinsic host-classification of the\nalready generated six types.  Neither \\(\\mathfrak{so}(4,1)\\) nor\nits noncompact finite-dimensional action is introduced as a new physical\nmomentum group or a faithful unitary finite-carrier operation constructor.\n\\end{proposition}\n\\begin{proof}\nThe first bracket is Lemma~\\ref{p2b:lem:canonical-bracket-image}.\nDirect differentiation of \\(K_A\\) and \\(G_u\\) gives the other two.\nThe injective map\n\\[\n K_A\\longmapsto\\begin{pmatrix}-A&0\\\\0&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad\n G_u\\longmapsto\\begin{pmatrix}0&u/\\Rmom\\\\u^\\top/\\Rmom&0\\end{pmatrix}\n\\]\npreserves the three brackets, and its image is the standard\n\\(\\mathfrak{so}(4,1)\\) block presentation.  The four gradients have\n\\((\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\)-type; the six Killing fields decompose as\n\\((1,0)\\oplus(0,1)\\).  Expanding the symmetric square of the two\nchiral defining modules proves the final representation identity.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Coordinate-algebra blocks versus geometric type blocks]\n\\label{p2b:rem:conformal-block-compatibility}\nThe geometric decomposition\n\\(\\mathbf1\\oplus\\mathfrak c_{\\mathbb C}\\oplus S\\)\norganizes \\(\\mathcal H_1\\) into dimensions \\(11+4\\).\nWhere the separately constituted intrinsic coordinate tuple and its\ncompletion hypotheses produce\n\\(\\mathcal A_D\\cong M_{11}(\\mathbb C)\\oplus M_4(\\mathbb C)\\),\nthose block sizes agree with the geometric organization.  Matrix\nsimplicity and the dimension \\(137=11^2+4^2\\) depend on the separate\ncoordinate-intertwiner/word calculation, not on the decomposition\n\\(11+4\\) alone, and do not select a physical operation or state.\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Maximal exact unital scalar derivation subalgebra]\n\\label{p2b:prop:maximal-finite-scalar-action}\nSet \\(\\mathcal P_1:=E_0\\oplus E_1\\subset C^\\infty(S^3(\\Rmom))\\).\nFor a smooth-host field \\(X\\in\\mathfrak c\\), let\n\\(\\delta_X(h)=X(h)\\) be its \\emph{ordinary} scalar derivation.  Then\n\\[\n \\delta_X(\\mathcal P_1)\\subseteq\\mathcal P_1\n \\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad X\\in\\mathcal K_{\\rm Kill}.\n\\]\nThis is the maximal exact action \\emph{among fields in}\n\\(\\mathfrak c\\), conditional only on taking \\(\\mathcal P_1\\) as the\nspecified scalar-operation target; the proposition does not assert that\nthe physical operation grammar has selected that target.\n\\end{proposition}\n\\begin{proof}\nWrite \\(X=K_A+G_u\\).  A Killing field preserves \\(E_0\\) and\n\\(E_1\\), since \\(K_A(f_v)=-f_{Av}\\).\nOn the other hand,\n\\[\n G_u(f_v)=u\\cdot v-\\frac{f_uf_v}{\\Rmom^2}.\n\\]\nIf \\(u\\ne0\\), take \\(v=u\\).  The traceless quadratic harmonic part of\n\\(f_u^2\\) is nonzero; the Killing term has degree one and cannot\ncancel it.  Thus \\(X\\) fails to preserve \\(\\mathcal P_1\\).\n\\end{proof}"
  },
